errors.description: Model incorrectly identified the colors and face assignments of the target cube, hallucinating faces (e.g., red, white, light blue) that do not appear on any of the 6 cubes shown in the video. errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: 'The cube shown has: Green on the left. Yellow on the front. Blue on the top. Red on the right. White on the back. Light blue on the bottom.'

errors.description: Model claims all four options match the cube, which is logically impossible for a multiple-choice question with a single correct answer. This indicates a failure to compare nets against the actual cube configuration or to recognize that cube nets must satisfy spatial constraints (e.g., opposite faces cannot be adjacent in the net).
errors.evidence_quote: Model trace: 'All options A, B, C, and D match the cube shown in the video.'

errors.description: Model incorrectly binds non-existent attributes (red, white, light blue) to the cube’s faces, and then incorrectly maps those hallucinated attributes to all four net options, failing to distinguish between them.

analysis_result.analysis: The model fundamentally misperceives the cube’s face colors, inventing red, white, and light blue faces that are not present in the video. This leads to a cascade of reasoning errors: it falsely concludes that all options match the cube, which violates basic logic and spatial constraints of cube nets. The error originates in perception (misidentifying colors) and propagates into grounding (wrong attribute binding) and reasoning (failing to distinguish between mutually exclusive options).
